note: Re-judged 2026-11-14 at 5d862bbab9 by an independent auditor who authored none of the changes named. RFC 9687 Section 4.3, SendHoldTimer_Expires (Event 29): "drops the TCP connection," is one action of the list the local system performs. The row gained a third tagged unit, TestSendHoldExpiryClosesBehindStuckWriter (session_wedge_test.go, positive), read whole with its helpers. It brings a real Session to Established over a net.Pipe with Run executing and the Send Hold Timer on the real clock (wedgeSendHold 5s; only the FSM timers are on a fake clock that is never advanced, so no KEEPALIVE moves the deadline and no hold timer closes the session). It takes writeMu as a stuck writer holds it, requires sendHoldDeadline non-zero so the expiry is still to come and must meet the held path, then requires the peer end's read to end with io.EOF within the time left to that deadline plus holdExpiryNotifyDeadline (1s) plus wedgeSlack (2s), all before the path is released. Only ze closing its end gives the peer io.EOF; a still-open socket is t.Fatal, and any other read error fails the ErrorIs. So it fails when the expiry waits on the write path for its optional NOTIFICATION or for a flush, which is the defect 1c6795e9e4 removed, and when the close step closes nothing. The producer was read: sendHoldTimerExpired bounds the NOTIFICATION by holdExpiryNotifyDeadline and calls closeConnWithin, which does not wait again after a NOTIFICATION that met the held path and then calls dropConn (expire the write deadline, close the socket). The claim states what the body asserts and no more: closure seen as EOF at the peer, bounded from the expiry, with the path held. The later assertions (Run returns ErrSendHoldTimerExpired, FSM Idle) are outside the claim and outside this row. Its discrimination record names the break of dropConn's body; I did not run it. The two earlier units in rfc9687_test.go are unchanged since their judgement and were not re-read: the check reports neither as moved, and their recorded judgement stands, with one correction to its wording: the expiry now reaches the close through closeConnWithin, not closeConn. The pair holds: the negative unit keeps the session and its transport intact one nanosecond short of expiry. No test or record ran for this rejudgment. Verdict unchanged: enforced.
